subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Messages We've Sent to Space
description: A short lesson to help you apply Messages We've Sent to Space.

hook.text: Humans haven't just listened—we've also sent messages into space, hoping someone might be out there to receive them.

buildup.text: The Arecibo message was beamed toward a star cluster in 1974. It encoded information about humans in binary code.

discovery.text: The Voyager Golden Records carry sounds, images, and music from Earth. They're now in interstellar space, still traveling.

twist.text: Some scientists argue against sending messages. If hostile aliens exist, broadcasting our location could be dangerous.

climax.text: Our radio signals have been leaking into space for over a century. Any nearby civilization could already know we're here.

punchline.text: We've been broadcasting for a century. If anyone's listening, they already know.

quiz.question: What concern do some scientists have about sending messages into space?
options: Broadcasting our location could be dangerous if hostile alien civilizations exist
The messages travel too slowly to ever reach another star system
Radio waves cannot pass through interstellar dust clouds

details.summary: Humanity has deliberately sent messages to potential alien recipients: the Arecibo Message (1974) beamed at a star cluster, the Voyager Golden Records carrying sounds and images of Earth, and various METI (Messaging Extraterrestrial Intelligence) transmissions targeted at nearby stars.
details.whyItMatters: These messages raise profound questions about representing humanity to unknown recipients and whether broadcasting our existence is wise. They're both scientific experiments and cultural milestones reflecting how we see ourselves.
takeaways: The Arecibo Message was beamed at a star cluster in 1974
Voyager Golden Records carry sounds and images from Earth
METI transmissions have targeted several nearby star systems

faq.question: What is on the Voyager Golden Record?
faq.answer: Sounds of Earth (thunder, whale songs, music from Bach to Chuck Berry), greetings in 55 languages, 115 images of humans, nature, and civilization, and encoded audio. A pulsar map shows Earth's location. Both Voyager probes carry identical gold-plated copper records.

faq.question: Could any alien actually decode our messages?
faq.answer: The Arecibo Message encodes information in binary assuming mathematical universality. The Voyager Record includes instructions for playback on its cover. Whether an alien intelligence could decode these is unknown — but mathematics and physics are thought to be universal language foundations.
